title: The Palantir-based DAR software identifies the author of an emailed amok threat against Siegen's city administration in fractions of a second and 51 of about 100 participants in a Duisburg shooting (28 October 2022)
summary: NRW Interior Ministry, 28 Oct 2022: Palantir-based DAR resolved an amok-threat email against Siegen's city administration in seconds and identified 51 of about 100 people at a Duisburg clan shooting.
account: On 28 October 2022 North Rhine-Westphalia's Interior Ministry said DAR, the police's Palantir software, played a central role in several recent cases (WELT; RP Online, 28 October 2022). In October someone had emailed the Siegen city administration announcing an amok attack over the city's 'topless' permission for swimming pools; the ministry said the email address revealed the suspect via Palantir in fractions of a second. After a shooting in Duisburg-Hamborn between a Turkish-Arab clan and the Hells Angels that injured four people, a Duisburg investigator said police quickly identified 51 of the roughly 100 participants, 49 of them assigned to rival groups, about 20 minutes each (RP Online; WELT). Interior Minister Herbert Reul told the Landtag's interior committee on 27 October that DAR links the weapons register, residents' registration, the police case system and the wanted-persons portal; the ministry puts the 2019-2025 cost at about 39 million euros, and the opposition attacks it on data-protection and cost grounds (WELT).
purpose: DAR was procured to let North Rhine-Westphalia police search and link entries across police and administrative databases during investigations; identifying suspects from an email address or from a nickname and phone number was that purpose.
system: DAR (Datenbankübergreifende Recherche und Analyse), Palantir software used by North Rhine-Westphalia police
deployer: North Rhine-Westphalia police, under the NRW Ministry of the Interior (contract since 2019)

ratings.reason: NRW police resolved an amok-threat email address to a person in fractions of a second and identified 51 of about 100 shooting participants at about 20 minutes each, per the ministry and a Duisburg investigator; no comparison with conventional methods, and no charges or convictions, are reported.

Siegen's administration and public had the author of a threatened amok attack identified, but the sources do not say whether the threat was credible, whether the person was charged, or what harm was averted.

ai_role.statement: The fetched reports describe DAR as software that links entries across the weapons register, residents' registration data, the police case system and the wanted-persons portal; none mentions machine learning, and the minister's own description is of plain linking, while the Monitor labels it an AI system. On the ministry's account the software's contribution was speed of identification, from an email address in fractions of a second and about 20 minutes per shooting participant; whether manual queries would have reached the same people, more slowly, is not addressed, and the claims come from the deployer's ministry and an unnamed investigator.

produced_by: Police and administrative databases (weapons register, residents' registration, case-processing system, wanted-persons portal) linked in one Palantir-based search
An identifier from the case, such as an email address, a nickname or a phone number, that matches an entry somewhere in the linked data
must_hold: The person already appears in one of the linked databases; the system links records, it does not generate new ones
Investigators have lawful access to the linked registers; the opposition contests the arrangement on data-protection grounds
Licensing continues; the ministry puts the 2019-2025 cost at about 39 million euros
